newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura hopes for monthly profit from April onward.
newsitem.headline: Nomura hopes for monthly profit from April onward.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it hopes to post a monthly parent current profit in April 1997 and succeeding months.

Takamichi Arata, a Nomura director, told a news conference that while the brokerage's revenues had been hit hard by a scandal revealed on March 6 involving suspected illegal deals linked to a racketeer, its efforts to cut operating expenditures were expected to help it post a monthly profit in April and thereafter in fiscal 1997/98.
He said Nomura was cutting its monthly operating expenditures to between 20.2 and 20.3 billion yen per month in April, down two billion from the previous month.
He added that monthly operating expenditure in April would be 22 percent below a peak of 26 billion yen five years ago.
Arata said that in the last quarter of fiscal 1996/97, Nomura's current profit was more than 20 billion yen.
In March, however, current profit was about half the usual monthly levels.
Arata attributed the decline in profits to the recent scandal.
"As one might expect, the scandal has had an effect (on our profits)," Arata said.
He added that Nomura's brokerage commissions and its share of the underwriting market had fallen in the wake of the scandal.
He said, however, that it was difficult to calculate the extent of the impact.

Earlier on Thursday, Nomura reported a 124.19 billion yen parent current profit in the year to March 31, 1997, although it posted a parent net loss of 271.51 billion yen due to financial support it extended to a troubled non-bank financial affiliate.
